whatThisIs: A corpus-wide measurement of the text a composed PDF actually delivers to a participant. It repairs nothing and promotes nothing. Its output is a worklist: which families ship unreadable text, which are clean, and which cohorts share one root cause.

instrument.principle: Measure the width of every whitespace-free token in the delivered text using the renderer's own font metrics. A hard split is invisible to a page-line census, a completeness counter and a raster gate, because the page is full, every character is present and the ink is where ink belongs. Only the token measurement sees it.
instrument.generalisedFrom: FIX17, which found a chopped citation URL at 467.32pt against a 468pt column in the Oklahoma trafficking family.

rendererGeometry.uniformityCheck: All 91 scripts carrying renderComposedPdf were read: every one carries fontSize 11, width 612, margin 72 and StandardFonts.TimesRoman. The column is 468pt corpus-wide, so one instrument measures every copy.

instrument.composedPageDetection: A drawn line is composer-origin if it sits at x = 72 exactly, at size 11 exactly, on the 14.5pt ladder descending from y = 720. This separates composed text from filled official-form text inside the same assembled packet, so an official form's own typography is never measured against the composer's column.

hardSplitTest.why: The faulty splitToken emits the maximal prefix that fits, so its chunk width W satisfies W <= 468 and W + width(next glyph) > 468. The widest Times-Roman glyph at 11pt is 10.384pt, so a hard-split fragment lands in (457.62, 468] by construction.
corroborationRequired: the fragment is followed by further text, i.e. the token resumes
appending the next printed glyph would have overflowed the column - the signature of a cut, not merely a wide token
the fragment does not end on one of the token's own separators ( : _ / . - ), which is where the repaired splitToken breaks
hardSplitTest.falseNegativeAudit: Five families whose widest token lands inside the band were not flagged. Each was inspected by hand: four break on their own hyphen (NV, TN, WV, OK) and are readable, and one (RI ri_deferred_sentence) is a whole 459.74pt route key that was never split. No false negatives found.
hardSplitTest.bandSeparationEvidence: Across the 122 composed-shipping families the widest token per family is bimodal: 101 families top out at or below 456.26pt, 21 land inside the cut band at 464.38pt or above. Nothing sits between 456.26pt and 464.38pt. The band is not an arbitrary threshold.

defectClasses.A_hard_split: a whitespace-free token cut at the margin rather than at a break a reader can read across
defectClasses.B_page_content: a page whose entire content is the internal route key, an empty page, or a page carrying fewer lines than a real page of content
defectClasses.C_block_integrity: a stranded trailer, a labelled value widowed across a page break, or a closing execution block orphaned from the signature line it executes
defectClasses.D_census: thin pages (under 8 drawn lines) that are the ordinary tail of a long component. Recorded as census, NOT asserted as a defect, because calling a short tail page a defect would inflate the worklist.

denominator.statedPlainly: 245 census-v1 families exist. 122 of them ship a composed PDF. Across those 122 the sweep read 324 delivered fixture PDFs, 2,658 pages of which 2,158 carry composer-drawn text, 53,447 composed lines, and measured 524,791 whitespace-free tokens against the 468pt column.

codeLevelCopyCensus.note: How many copies of the faults exist in code, which is a different and larger number than how many families actually ship a visible defect.
codeLevelCopyCensus.reading: 89 of 98 splitToken copies still carry the original char-by-char splitter. Only 9 carry the separator-aware repair.

positiveControl.why: A universal negative is the shape of a broken denominator. Before any corpus claim is made, the instrument must separate two states of the same four families: repaired (clean) and pre-repair (dirty). If it cannot, it is measuring nothing.
positiveControl.method: The four already-repaired families were measured twice with the identical instrument: once on the delivered bytes at the Captain tip, and once on the bytes recovered from git history immediately before each repair landed (FIX16 parent 46531b3085acbc990ea6fb0dfe958773a44d8b45, FIX17 parent 1cc823b6ce1f82a1c3bf64b17ed992a79d03423d).
positiveControl.verdict: PASSED on the hard-split class, which is the class the instrument exists for: 122 hard splits across three families before, zero after, in all four families.

families.corroboration: 2355 tokens measured before and 2355 after. An identical token count on both sides of a repair is independent confirmation of FIX16's and FIX17's claim that nothing was dropped to make anything fit - only breaks moved.

Its repair was the block rule, and the block classes discriminate it: 24 defects before, 0 after.

residueFoundInTheTwoFIX16Families.finding: rcap-ok-custom-pleading and rcap-wa-custom-pleading-clean-tracks come back clean on the hard-split class but NOT clean overall: OK still ships 8 orphaned execution blocks and WA 2, plus 2 fragment pages.
residueFoundInTheTwoFIX16Families.itIsNotAnInstrumentFault: FIX16 repaired these two with Rule 1 (gather the contact block) and its trailer sole-occupant pull-down. FIX17 later established that Rule 1 alone leaves the gathered block on a page of its own with nothing to say what it executes, and added Rule 1b for that. Rule 1b was applied to North Dakota only. Reading the builders confirms it: rcap-ok-custom-pleading and rcap-wa-custom-pleading-clean-tracks carry soleOccupant and the separator-aware splitToken but contain no Rule 1b; rcap-nd-custom-pleading carries Rule 1b and comes back clean.
residueFoundInTheTwoFIX16Families.consequence: FIX17's Rule 1b never travelled back to the two families FIX16 repaired. That is a named, one-line-of-reasoning repair for a known cohort, not a discovery.

familiesMeasuredAndClean.note: These shipped a composed PDF, were measured by the same instrument, and carry no class A, B or C defect. Listed so a later reader knows the sweep covered them rather than skipped them.

couldNotMeasure.why: They are Judicial Council forms carried into the fixture set unchanged and encrypted by the issuer. pdf-lib loads them with ignoreEncryption but their content streams cannot be walked, so no text can be extracted from them.
couldNotMeasure.whyItDoesNotDentTheDenominator: All 74 belong to 8 California official-pdf-fill families, and those families have no composer at all: build-census-v1-ca-1203-4-set.mjs and its siblings contain no renderComposedPdf, no splitToken and no render* composer function, and their readable fixtures carry zero composer-drawn lines. They are outside the composed-PDF corpus entirely, so nothing composed went unmeasured.

cohorts.judgementOnHowManyOfTheNinetyAreAffected: Of 122 families shipping a composed PDF, 40 carry at least one class A/B/C defect and 82 are clean. The right way to read that is NOT "40 of 90 copies are broken". 89 of 98 splitToken copies still carry the faulty splitter, so the code-level exposure is near-total; what varies is whether a family happens to contain a token long enough to reach the margin. 16 families actually ship a hard split, and in every one of them the chopped token is a route key or a citation URL, never body prose. The defect is therefore not randomly distributed: it fires wherever a route key exceeds roughly 458pt, which is a property of the route-key naming convention, not of the jurisdiction.

doTheyClusterByBuilderGeneration.answer: Yes, decisively, and this is the most useful axis.
doTheyClusterByBuilderGeneration.reading: 109 of 122 composed-shipping families are G0: original row-by-row pagination with the original char-by-char splitter. Every one of the 16 hard-split families is G0. The 4 repaired families are the only ones carrying the separator-aware splitter, and the single G3 (North Dakota, Rule 1b included) is the only family clean on every class by construction.

doTheyClusterByJurisdiction.answer: Weakly, and only as a shadow of the builder-host axis.
doTheyClusterByJurisdiction.reading: Georgia contributes 7 affected families and Rhode Island 4, but neither is a jurisdictional fact: all 7 Georgia families are built by build-census-v1-ga-host.mjs and 4 of the 5 Rhode Island families by build-census-v1-ri_decriminalized-set.mjs. Dispatching by state would split single-root cohorts across lanes and merge unrelated ones.

doTheyClusterByComponentKind.reading: 30 of 87 composed-shipping custom-pleading families are affected and 11 of 35 official-pdf-fill families are - close to the same rate. An assembled official-form packet composes its own instruction and cover pages through the same renderer, so component kind predicts nothing.

sharedComposerHosts.finding: The corpus is NOT ninety independent copies. 41 of the 122 composed-shipping families already reach the composer through one of 7 shared host modules; 81 own a private copy.
sharedComposerHosts.whyThisMatters: Each shared host is a single-edit cohort. Repairing scripts/rcap-custom-pleading/composed-family-host.mjs alone reaches 13 families; build-census-v1-ga-host.mjs reaches 9 and carries 7 of the affected families. Every one of the 7 hosts carries the original char-by-char splitToken, so none of them has been repaired yet.

dispatchWorklist.oneRoot: the char-by-char splitToken inside a module that many families import
dispatchWorklist.repair: Carry FIX16's separator-aware splitToken into each host. One edit per host, 7 edits, reaching 41 families.
dispatchWorklist.riskToCurrentlyCleanFamilies: Low but not nil: the separator-aware splitter changes where a break falls in any family whose route key exceeds the column, so a currently-clean family sharing the host can move bytes. Every host's dependants must be rebuilt and re-measured together, and re-rastered.

dispatchWorklist.oneRoot: FIX16's Rule 1 gathers the closing contact block but leaves it alone on a page; FIX17's Rule 1b fixes exactly that and was applied to North Dakota only
dispatchWorklist.repair: Port Rule 1b, conditional exactly as FIX17 made it, into the two FIX16 builders.
dispatchWorklist.riskToCurrentlyCleanFamilies: None outside the two families; Rule 1b is per-builder and fires only where the settled layout actually splits the unit.

dispatchWorklist.oneRoot: the same char-by-char splitToken, in a builder no other family imports
dispatchWorklist.repair: Same one-function replacement, once per builder.

dispatchWorklist.oneRoot: row-by-row pagination with no block awareness, plus the route key being emitted as ordinary body text so it can become a page's sole occupant
dispatchWorklist.repair: Two separable moves. First, stop the route key being able to stand alone on a participant-facing page - that is the reasoning FIX16 transferred out of the Nevada patch, and it does not require block-aware pagination. Second, block-aware pagination for the fragment pages, which does.
dispatchWorklist.riskToCurrentlyCleanFamilies: Higher: block-aware pagination moves breaks in families that were never wrong. Do the route-key move first and re-measure before touching pagination.

sharedRendererConsolidation.question: Should the shared-renderer consolidation now go ahead?
sharedRendererConsolidation.fix17Position: Not yet - at least five pagination algorithms live in the copies, and three exist specifically to avoid moving content that was never wrong.
sharedRendererConsolidation.scan01Position: NOT YET AS ONE RENDERER, BUT THE PREMISE HAS CHANGED AND A NARROWER CONSOLIDATION SHOULD GO AHEAD NOW.
whatTheCorpusEvidenceAdds: The geometry is already universal. All 91 renderComposedPdf copies carry the identical font, size, page box and margin, so the 468pt column is corpus-wide. Nothing has to be reconciled there.

The corpus is not ninety independent copies. 41 of 122 composed-shipping families already import their composer from one of 7 shared hosts. Consolidation is not a new idea being introduced to this tree; it is a pattern already in production, unfinished.

The divergence is concentrated in pagination, not in splitting. 115 of 122 composed-shipping families carry the SAME char-by-char splitToken and only 4 carry the repair. There are not five splitters - there are two, and one of them is correct.

Only 13 of 122 composed-shipping families carry any pagination marker beyond the plain row-by-row default: 6 are block-aware, 3 carry Rule 1b or the sole-occupant pull-down, and the rest are G0. The five algorithms FIX17 counted are real, but they cover a small minority of families.

82 of 122 families are currently clean, and 71 of those are clean while carrying the faulty splitter - they simply have no token long enough to reach the margin. Any shared module that changes break behaviour must leave all 82 byte-identical, and the splitter change alone cannot disturb a family whose widest token is under 457pt. 101 of 122 families are in exactly that position.

judgement.goAheadNow: Consolidate splitToken alone, into one shared module, corpus-wide. This is tractable today and the data says so: one correct implementation already exists and is proven on four families; the column is universal; and it is provably inert in the 101 families whose widest token measures under the 457.62pt band floor. FIX17 already demonstrated the inertness argument on North Dakota by instrumenting a build and counting zero splitToken calls. That argument generalises, and this sweep supplies the per-family widest-token measurement that makes it checkable before any rebuild.
judgement.doNotDoYet: Do not subsume the five pagination algorithms into one module yet. North Dakota's per-component line-height parameter, Oklahoma's simulate-and-collapse, FIX16's block-gather with trailer pull-down, Nevada's component-level suppression and FIX17's conditional Rule 1b are not five ways of doing one thing; three of them exist specifically to avoid moving content that was never wrong, and Rule 1b is conditional precisely because an unconditional version cost the pardoned boundary packet a page for nothing. A shared paginator would have to reproduce all five behaviours exactly on 82 currently-clean families, and the only proof that it had would be a byte-identical rebuild of every one of them.
judgement.theTractabilityAnswerAsked: Is it tractable for a shared module to subsume five algorithms without moving a byte of any currently-clean family? On this evidence: not as one module today, but the problem is much smaller than ninety. Strip out splitToken - shared, safe, corpus-wide. Then the pagination question reduces to 13 families carrying a non-default algorithm plus the 7 shared hosts, and a shared paginator can be introduced host by host with the currently-clean dependants of that host as the byte-identity gate. That is a tractable sequence. A single big-bang renderer across 122 families is not.
sequence: 1. Shared splitToken module, corpus-wide. Gate: every family whose widest token is under 457.62pt must rebuild byte-identical. This sweep records that width per family.
2. Rule 1b into the two FIX16 families. Gate: only those two families move.
3. Route key may never be a page's sole occupant. Gate: the 17 route-key-only pages disappear and nothing else moves.
4. Shared paginator, host by host, starting with rcap-custom-pleading/composed-family-host.mjs. Gate: byte-identical rebuild of that host's currently-clean dependants.

whatThisSweepDoesNotEstablish: No verdict is issued and no route is opened or closed. This lane holds no grant and changed no family.

A clean result here means the delivered text carries no measurable hard split, route-key-only page, fragment page or broken block. It says nothing about legal correctness, source fidelity, visual review or raster state.
Thin pages under 8 drawn lines are recorded as census, not asserted as defects. A short page that is the tail of a long component is not by itself wrong.
The 74 encrypted California official forms were not read. They belong to families with no composer, so no composed text went unmeasured, but their contents are unexamined by this sweep.
Fixture bytes are what was measured. Whether a rebuild reproduces them is a separate question this lane did not run.
